game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Three dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (4 faces, each equally likely): 0, 1, 4, 10.
- Die 2 (8 faces, each equally likely): 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 4, 4, 9.
- Die 3 (8 faces, each equally likely): 0, 2, 7, 7, 8, 8, 9, 9.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
The contract's fair value is 12.5, and I'm quoting about 6.5 either side of it to cover the risk from informed traders.

**Fair value.** Each die's average is:
- Die 1: 3.75
- Die 2: 2.5
- Die 3: 6.25

So the expected sum is 12.5.

**Uncertainty.** Each die's variance is:
- Die 1: about 15.2
- Die 2: 8.5
- Die 3: about 9.9

That gives a total variance of about 33.6, so the settlement value has a standard deviation of about 5.8. This is the same size as the noise traders' spread.

**Spread choice.** I set the half-spread h as a multiple k of that standard deviation, σ = 5.8. Using a normal approximation, my net edge per side is proportional to 2k(1−Φ(k)) − φ(k). This is gains from noise traders minus losses to informed traders. It is positive and roughly flat for k between 1 and 1.5, with the best value near k ≈ 1.2. That gives h ≈ 6.5–7 around 12.5.

{"bid": 6.0, "ask": 19.0}

The informed buy at 19 moves my fair value up to about 17.3. I'm quoting a bid of 13 and an ask of 21.5 around that, kept wide because informed traders could hold either extreme.

**Prior.** The die means are 3.75, 2.5 and 6.25, so the prior expected sum is 12.5.

**Who buys at 19.**
- An informed trader buys only if the settlement value is above 19. With integer sums that means 20 or more, which has probability 31/256 ≈ 0.121.
- A noise trader buys if 12.5 plus noise exceeds 19. That needs a 1.12 standard-deviation move, so the probability is about 0.13.

**Update after the buy.**
- The chance the sum is 20 or more rises to about 0.54.
- If the sum is 20 or more, its expected value is about 22.4.
- Otherwise its expected value is about 11.1.
- The new public fair value is therefore about 0.54 × 22.4 + 0.46 × 11.1 ≈ 17.3.

**Quote.** The bid at 13 and ask at 21.5 sit on either side of 17.3. The posterior has two clusters: a high one around 20 to 28 and a low one around 11. Informed traders can hurt me on either side, so the quote stays wide. Noise traders still cross it reasonably often.

{"bid": 13, "ask": 21.5}

Fair value is about 17.8, but the value is probably either near 21 or near 13, so I'm quoting wide: bid 15.5, ask 22.

- **Prior:** The dice average 3.75, 2.5 and 6.25, so the sum starts at 12.5.
- **Quote 1 (bought at 19):** Only about 12% of outcomes settle above 19, and a noise trader values above 19 only about 13% of the time. That buy shifts roughly half the probability to outcomes above 19.
- **Quote 2 (no trade at 13 / 21.5):** This makes 13–21.5 more likely. Above 19 that means 20–21; below 19 it means 13–19.
- **Result:** Fair value is about 17.8, made up of two clusters:
  - about 56% weight near 21.7;
  - about 44% weight near 12.9.
- **Quote:** Because the two clusters are far apart, informed traders will hit whichever side is wrong. A wide quote around fair protects against that. I'm short 1, so I lean slightly upward.

{"bid": 15.5, "ask": 22}

Fair value is about 19.7, and I'll quote 18.0 bid / 21.4 ask around it.

**Fair value.** Die 1 is revealed as 10. Die 2 averages 2.5 and die 3 averages 6.25, so with no other information the sum would be 18.75.

**Updating on stage-1 trading.** I worked out the distribution of die 2 + die 3 (call it S) and weighted each value by how likely it made the stage-1 history:
- **Quote 1:** someone bought at 19, which favours S ≥ 10 (a total above 19).
- **Quote 2:** no trade at 13 / 21.5. If the counterparty was informed, that means a total between 13 and 21.5, so S between 3 and 11.
- **Quote 3:** no trade at 15.5 / 22. If informed, that means S between 6 and 12.

After this update, S averages about 9.7, so fair value is about 19.7. Most of the probability sits on totals between 17 and 21.

**Quote.**
- **Bid 18.0:** an informed seller only hits it about 14% of the time (when S ≤ 7). A noise trader sells at that price about 38% of the time, giving me about 1.7 of edge.
- **Ask 21.4:** an informed buyer only lifts it about 10% of the time (when S ≥ 12). A noise trader buys at that price about 39% of the time, giving me about 1.7 of edge.
- **Position:** I'm short 1, so I keep the ask a little closer to fair than the midpoint would suggest.

{"bid": 18.0, "ask": 21.4}

The posterior puts the settlement value at about **20.3**, so I quote 19.5 / 21.1 around it.

**Starting point.** Die 1 is 10. Die 2 averages 2.5 and die 3 averages 6.25, so with no trade information the value would be 18.75.

**What the trades tell us.** I updated the distribution of die 2 + die 3 (call it S) using each quote. An informed counterparty knows the true value; a noise trader trades at random around the public fair value.

- **Quote 1:** someone bought at 19 when the public fair value was 12.5. A noise trader only does that about 13% of the time, so this strongly favours S ≥ 10.
- **Quotes 2–4:** no trades at 13/21.5, 15.5/22 and 18/21.4. An informed counterparty would not trade if the value were inside each spread. The tightest of these says S is likely between 8 and 11.

**Posterior.**

| S | Value | Probability |
|---|---|---|
| 11 | 21 | about 51% |
| 10 | 20 | about 29% |
| 9 | 19 | about 9% |
| 8 | 18 | about 7% |
| Other | | about 4% |

The expected value is about 20.3.

**Quote.** A bid of 19.5 only loses to an informed seller when the value is 18 or 19, about 16% of the time. An ask of 21.1 only loses to an informed buyer when the value is 22 or more, about 2%. Noise traders centred near 20.3 give me edge on both sides. My position of -1 leaves plenty of room either way.

{"bid": 19.5, "ask": 21.1}

Die 1 = 10, so the value is 10 + S, where S is the sum of dice 2 and 3. Before trading, E[S] = 2.5 + 6.25 = 8.75.

**Updating on the history**
- Quote 4: no trade at 18 / 21.4. That makes S between 8 and 11 more likely.
- Quote 5: someone sold to me at 19.5. That points to S ≤ 9.
- After both updates, E[S] ≈ 8.4, so the public fair value is about 18.4.
- Most of the probability now sits on a settlement of 18 (about 29%) or 19 (about 40%). There is a low tail at 17 or below (about 13.5%) and a high tail at 20 or above (about 17%).

**Choosing the quote**
- **Ask:** quoting near the fair value loses on balance. Informed buyers take me out whenever the value is 20 or more. As the ask rises, the expected profit from noise buyers outweighs that loss. Expected profit levels off at roughly 22–23.
- **Bid:** a bid near 18 gets hit by informed sellers whenever the value is in the low tail. Lowering the bid to about 15 makes noise sellers worth more than informed losses.
- I am flat, and die 3 is revealed next stage, so there is no inventory reason to skew the quote.

{"bid": 15, "ask": 22}

Die 1 = 10 and die 3 = 8 are revealed, so settlement is **18 + die 2**.

**Valuing die 2.** Its prior mean is 2.5. The trading history changes that:
- In stage 1, someone bought at 19. That points to a higher total, so die 2 ≥ 2 if the buyer was informed.
- Quote 2 had no trade with an ask of 21.5. That points to die 2 ≤ 2.
- Quote 4 had no trade with an ask of 21.4. That also points to die 2 ≤ 2.
- In stage 2, someone sold at 19.5. That points to die 2 ≤ 1.

**Posterior.** I weighted each die 2 value by how likely the observed trades were under it. The weights assume half the counterparties are informed and noise traders' valuations are centred on the public fair value. This gives roughly:
- 0: 41%
- 1: 13%
- 2: 41%
- 4: 4%
- 9: under 1%

Expected die 2 is about 1.15, so fair value is about **19.15**.

**Choosing the quotes.** I compared the expected profit from noise trades with the expected loss to informed traders at different prices.
- Settlement is almost never above 22, so asks around 23–24 lose very little to informed traders. The best net gain is about 0.49 near 23.5.
- Settlement can never be below 18, so any bid below 18 is safe from informed sellers. The best is about 0.48–0.49 near 15–15.5.

I'll quote slightly tighter than that so noise traders still trade with me.

{"bid": 15.5, "ask": 23.0}

Die 1 = 10 and die 3 = 8, so the settlement is 18 plus die 2. That gives 18, 19, 20, 22 or 27.

**Updating on quote 7.** My 15.5 / 23 quote drew no trade.
- An informed trader would have bought if the value were 27, so no trade cuts the weight on 27.
- A noise trader values the contract at public fair plus noise with standard deviation 5.8. Before quote 7, public fair was 18 + 2.5 = 20.5. At that level, a noise trader stays out about 47% of the time.

Updated probabilities:

| Settlement | Probability |
|---|---|
| 18 | ≈ 0.41 |
| 19 | ≈ 0.14 |
| 20 | ≈ 0.14 |
| 22 | ≈ 0.27 |
| 27 | ≈ 0.04 |

Fair value ≈ 19.9.

**Choosing the ask.**
- Any ask of 22 or higher can only lose to an informed buyer if the value is 27, which now has about 4% probability.
- Each half-unit is the 50% chance the counterparty is that type.

| Ask | Expected edge |
|---|---|
| 23 | 0.5 × 3.1 × 0.30 (noise) − 0.5 × 4 × 0.044 (informed) ≈ 0.37 |
| 24 | ≈ 0.43 |
| 25 | ≈ 0.44 (peak) |
| 26 | ≈ 0.43 |

The edge peaks around an ask of 25, so I'll quote 24.9.

**Choosing the bid.**
- Any bid of 18 or lower faces no informed sellers, because the settlement can't be below 18.
- The noise-trader edge peaks between bids of 15 and 16 (about 0.49), so I'll bid 15.6.

{"bid": 15.6, "ask": 24.9}

Only die 2 is still hidden, so the contract settles at 18 + die 2. That gives possible values of 18, 18, 18, 19, 20, 22, 22 and 27, with a prior mean of 20.5.

**What the last two quotes tell us.** There were no trades at 15.5/23 or at 15.6/24.9. An informed trader holding a value of 27 would have bought at either ask. So the no-trades make 27 much less likely: its relative likelihood drops to about 0.12. With that update the public fair value is about 19.7.

**Choosing the ask.** I compared the expected profit at several asks:

| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 22 | ≈0.37 |
| 24 | ≈0.47 |
| 25 | ≈0.46 |

The only informed buyer left is the unlikely value of 27. Noise buyers pay well above fair value, so a wide ask near 24 does best.

**Choosing the bid.** Any bid above 18 invites informed sellers, since 18 is the most likely value. A bid at 18.5 is worth only about 0.15. Bids between about 15 and 16 earn roughly 0.48–0.49 from noise sellers alone, so I'll bid around 15.5.

{"bid": 15.5, "ask": 24.2}

game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Three dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (6 faces, each equally likely): 5, 5, 6, 7, 8, 11.
- Die 2 (4 faces, loaded): 2 (prob 2/5), 2 (prob 1/10), 6 (prob 1/5), 8 (prob 3/10).
- Die 3 (4 faces, each equally likely): 7, 7, 8, 10.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
The contract's expected value is 19.6, so I centre the quote there with a half-spread of about 3.5.

**Expected value of the sum**
- Die 1: (5+5+6+7+8+11)/6 = 7.
- Die 2: 2×0.5 + 6×0.2 + 8×0.3 = 4.6.
- Die 3: (7+7+8+10)/4 = 8.
- Total: 7 + 4.6 + 8 = 19.6.

**Spread of the sum**
- Die 1 variance is 4.33, die 2 is 7.24 and die 3 is 1.5.
- Total variance is 13.07, so the standard deviation is about 3.6.

**Choosing the half-spread h**
- Treat the noise traders' valuations and the settlement value as roughly Normal, both with standard deviation about 3.6.
- Per side, I earn about h for each trade at my price. I lose to informed traders when the true value lies beyond my quote.
- This gives expected profit per side of about h(1−Φ(z)) − 0.35·3.6·φ(z), where z = h/3.6.
- The maximum is near z = 1, so h ≈ 3.5.
- That puts the bid at about 19.6 − 3.5 = 16.1 and the ask at about 19.6 + 3.5 = 23.1.

{"bid": 16.1, "ask": 23.1}

Fair value after the first trade is about 21.5, so I'm quoting a bid of 18.8 and an ask of 24.0, with a slight upward skew because I'm short 1.

**Prior fair value.** The expected value of each die:
- Die 1 averages 42/6 = 7.
- Die 2 averages 2(0.5) + 6(0.2) + 8(0.3) = 4.6.
- Die 3 averages 32/4 = 8.

The prior fair value is therefore 7 + 4.6 + 8 = 19.6.

**Update from the buy at 23.1.**
- The chance the sum is 24 or more is about 0.142. In those cases the expected sum is about 25.56.
- A noise trader values the contract above 23.1 with probability P(Z > 0.97), about 0.166.
- Each outcome is weighted by 0.65 × 0.166 = 0.108 from noise traders. Outcomes of 24 or more get an extra 0.35 from informed traders.
- The new fair value is (0.108 × 19.6 + 0.35 × 0.142 × 25.56) / (0.108 + 0.35 × 0.142), which is about 21.5.

**Quote.** I keep a wide spread because 35% of counterparties are informed and the distribution is skewed.

{"bid": 18.8, "ask": 24.0}

Fair value is about 21.6, up from a prior mean of 19.6 after the trade history. I'm quoting 19.8 / 23.8, about 2 wide on each side and skewed slightly up because I'm short.

**Prior mean.** The three dice have expected values of 7, 4.6 and 8, so the sum starts at 19.6.

**Update from the history.** I worked out the full distribution of the sum and weighted each value by how likely the two quotes' outcomes were under it.
- **Quote 1:** someone bought at 23.1. An informed trader does this only if the sum is 24 or more, which has a prior probability of about 14%. A noise trader buys there about 17% of the time.
- **Quote 2:** nobody traded at 18.8 / 24. An informed trader stays out only if the sum is between 19 and 24.

Combining both updates gives a posterior fair value of about 21.6.

**Quote.** I'm short one unit, so I lean the quote slightly upward. Each side sits about 2 away from fair value to protect against informed traders, who arrive 35% of the time.

{"bid": 19.8, "ask": 23.8}

With die 1 revealed as 11, the public fair value is about 23.6, and the settlement value is clearly split into a low cluster and a high cluster.

**Settlement distribution given die 1 = 11**

Die 2 has a mean of 4.6 and die 3 has a mean of 8, so the fair value is 11 + 4.6 + 8 = 23.6. The possible settlement values are:

| Value | Probability |
|---|---|
| 20 | 0.25 |
| 21 | 0.125 |
| 23 | 0.125 |
| 24 | 0.10 |
| 25 | 0.05 |
| 26 | 0.15 |
| 27 | 0.125 |
| 29 | 0.075 |

**Choosing the ask**

For each candidate ask, I weighed noise-trader profit (0.65 weight) against losses to informed traders (0.35 weight):
- An ask of 24.1 has an expected profit of about -0.23. Informed buyers hit it too often.
- An ask of 25.9 makes about +0.26.
- An ask of 27.0 makes about +0.33. Informed traders only buy here when the value is 29, since a value of exactly 27 is not above the ask.
- An ask of 27.5 makes about +0.31.

**Choosing the bid**

- A bid of 20.0 makes about +0.37. No settlement value is below 20, so informed traders never sell to me there.
- A bid of 21.0 makes about +0.31, because informed sellers with a value of 20 now hit it.
- A bid of 19.5 makes about +0.34.

The best quote is a bid of 20.0 and an ask of 27.0.

{"bid": 20.0, "ask": 27.0}

With die 1 revealed as 11, the remaining value comes from dice 2 and 3.

**Possible settlements:**
- If die 2 shows 2 (probability 0.5), the sum is 20, 20, 21 or 23.
- If die 2 shows 6 (probability 0.2), the sum is 24, 24, 25 or 27.
- If die 2 shows 8 (probability 0.3), the sum is 26, 26, 27 or 29.
- The prior mean is 11 + 4.6 + 8 = 23.6.

**What the last quote tells us:** Nobody traded at 20 / 27. An informed trader would have bought if the value were 29, so a 29 is now a little less likely. This moves the fair value down slightly, to about 23.4.

**Choosing the quote:**
- **Bid at 20.0:** Informed traders never sell at this price, because the lowest possible value is 20 and they only sell if their value is below my bid. Noise traders still sell often enough to give about +0.38 expected per quote.
- **Ask near 26.9:** The informed traders who would buy (values 27 or 29) are rare, so the expected loss to them is small, about 0.04. The expected gain from noise traders is about 0.38. That nets out to roughly +0.34.

{"bid": 20.0, "ask": 26.9}

Die 1 came up 11, so the settlement value is 11 + die 2 + die 3. The possible totals are:

| Die 2 | Die 3 = 7 | Die 3 = 8 | Die 3 = 10 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 20 | 21 | 23 |
| 6 | 24 | 25 | 27 |
| 8 | 26 | 27 | 29 |

**What the stage 2 trades tell me**
- **Quote 4 (20 / 27), no trade:** an informed trader stays out unless the value is 29, so this slightly lowers the chance of 29.
- **Quote 5 (20 / 26.9), someone bought at 26.9:** an informed trader buys only if the value is 27 or 29, so this makes those totals more likely.

**Updated beliefs**
- Value 27 is now about 34% likely.
- Value 29 is about 11% likely.
- The low values (20, 21 and 23) together are about 34% likely.
- My fair value estimate is about **24.8**.

**Ask side**
- At 27.0 or above, an informed trader buys only when the value is 29.
- Expected profit is fairly flat between asks of 27 and 28, at roughly 0.31 to 0.35 per quote.
- I chose 27.5, which is around the best in that range.

**Bid side**
- At 21.0, an informed trader sells only when the value is 20, and loses me just 1.
- Noise sellers still trade often enough at 21 to make this about 0.30 expected per quote.
- That beats a bid of 20 (about 0.29) and a bid of 22 (about 0.25).
- Buying would also reduce my short position.

{"bid": 21.0, "ask": 27.5}

Dice 1 and 2 are revealed, so the known part is 11 + 8 = 19. Only die 3 is still unknown, so the settlement is 19 plus die 3.

**Settlement outcomes**
- Die 3 = 7 (probability 1/2): settles at 26.
- Die 3 = 8 (probability 1/4): settles at 27.
- Die 3 = 10 (probability 1/4): settles at 29.
- Fair value = 27.0, and no trades have happened yet this stage to move it.

**Choosing the ask**
- If the ask is above 29, informed traders never buy from me.
- Noise traders still buy when 27 plus their noise exceeds the ask.
- Expected profit from noise traders is 0.65 × P(buy) × (ask − 27). This is roughly 0.397 at an ask of 29.6 to 29.8, which is the best.
- That beats quoting 28.9, which earns about 0.36 because informed traders buy when the value is 29.

**Choosing the bid**
- If the bid is below 26, informed traders never sell to me.
- Expected profit from noise traders is 0.65 × P(sell) × (27 − bid). This peaks at about 0.398 with a bid of 24.3.
- Any bid above 26 loses money, because informed traders sell whenever the value is 26, which happens half the time.

My position limits allow a trade on either side.

{"bid": 24.3, "ask": 29.7}

Dice 1 and 2 are revealed (11 + 8 = 19), so settlement is 19 plus die 3. That gives 26 with probability 1/2, 27 with 1/4 and 29 with 1/4. The expected settlement is 27.0. The no-trade at quote 7 (24.3 / 29.7) tells us little, so the public fair value stays about 27.

**Ask side:** An informed trader only buys if the settlement value is above my ask, which can only happen when it is 29. An ask at 29 or higher therefore avoids informed buyers entirely. For noise buyers, my expected profit is 0.65 × P(noise valuation > ask) × (ask − 27). This peaks at about 27 + 2.7 = 29.7, giving roughly 0.40 per quote.

**Bid side:** An informed trader only sells if the settlement value is below my bid, so any bid at or below 26 avoids informed sellers. The noise-trader calculation mirrors the ask side, so the best bid is about 27 − 2.7 = 24.3. That is safely below 26.

My position limits are not a constraint here, so I quote symmetrically around 27.

{"bid": 24.3, "ask": 29.7}

Dice 1 and 2 are revealed, so the known part of the sum is 11 + 8 = 19. Die 3 is 7, 7, 8 or 10, so settlement is 26 (prob 1/2), 27 (1/4) or 29 (1/4). The expected value is 27.

**What the history tells us:** An informed trader never trades against 24.3/29.7, because every possible settlement value lies inside that range. So the buy at 29.7 must have come from a noise trader, and the public fair value stays at 27.

**Ask:** Above 29, informed traders never buy, so only noise traders (valuation 27 plus noise, sd 3.6) lift the ask. Expected profit is 0.65 × P(noise > a) × (a − 27). This peaks at about 0.40, for any ask between roughly 29.6 and 29.8. Lower asks also attract informed buyers when the value is 29, which costs more than the extra noise flow brings in.

**Bid:** Below 26, informed traders never sell. Noise-trader profit is 0.65 × P(noise < b) × (27 − b), which peaks at about 0.40 for bids near 24.2–24.5. Above 26, informed sellers whenever the value is 26 (prob 1/2) make the bid much worse.

**Position:** I am at −2, so either fill leaves me at −3, within limits.

{"bid": 24.3, "ask": 29.7}

game.title: Dice sum
game.description:
Three dice are rolled independently. Repeated numbers are separate faces.
- Die 1 (4 faces, each equally likely): 1, 5, 7, 10.
- Die 2 (6 faces, each equally likely): 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 12.
- Die 3 (8 faces, each equally likely): 0, 0, 1, 6, 6, 7, 11, 11.
game.contract: The contract settles at the sum of all the dice.

info.raw:
Fair value is the expected sum of the three dice, which is **16**.

- Die 1: (1+5+7+10)/4 = 5.75
- Die 2: (1+2+3+4+8+12)/6 = 5.00
- Die 3: (0+0+1+6+6+7+11+11)/8 = 5.25

The settlement value has a standard deviation of about 6.6, and 20% of counterparties know the exact outcome. A half-spread of about 4 balances the profit from noise traders against losses to informed traders. So I quote 12.0 bid and 20.0 ask.

{"bid": 12.0, "ask": 20.0}

Fair value is about 16.0, and the quote-1 no-trade does not change it, so I centre on 16.

- **Expected value:** die 1 averages 5.75, die 2 averages 5.0 and die 3 averages 5.25. The sum is 16.0.
- **Uncertainty:** the settlement value has a standard deviation of about 6.6. That is about the same as the noise traders' spread.
- **Effect of the no-trade:** quote 1 at 12/20 saw no trade. That slightly suggests the value lies inside that range. It is roughly symmetric around 16, so it leaves the fair value where it is.
- **Spread:** informed traders know the exact sum, so I keep about ±3 around 16. That earns from noise traders while limiting what informed traders can take.

{"bid": 13, "ask": 19}

Fair value is about 17.5, a little above the prior expected sum of 16.

- **Prior expected sum:** the three dice average 5.75, 5 and 5.25, which gives 16. The standard deviation of the sum is about 6.6.
- **Quote 1:** there was no trade at 12/20, which tells us little.
- **Quote 2:** the counterparty bought at 19. Informed traders only buy there if the sum is above 19, so this pushes my estimate up to roughly 17.3–17.5.
- **Position:** I am short 1 unit. I centre my quote near 17.5, with a 3-point half-spread on each side to cover the risk of trading against informed counterparties.

{"bid": 14.5, "ask": 20.5}

I put fair value at about 18.6 and quote 16.0 / 21.5, leaning slightly upward because I am short 2.

**Starting estimate.** With die 3 revealed as 6, the starting expected sum is 5.75 + 5 + 6 = 16.75.

**What the trading history says.** Two counterparties bought at 19 and at 20.5. An informed trader buys only when the true value is above the ask. That makes high totals more likely than the plain average suggests.

- **Buy at 19:** high outcomes are about 1.8 times as likely as low ones. That means die 1 + die 2 above 13.
- **Buy at 20.5:** high outcomes are about 1.9 times as likely as low ones. That means die 1 + die 2 of 15 or more.
- **No trade at 12/20:** this slightly lowers the weight on totals above 20 and below 12.

I weighted the 24 possible die 1 + die 2 combinations by these factors. Their expected sum comes out at about 12.7, so fair value is about 18.6.

**Inventory.** Being short 2 means I would rather buy than sell, so I keep the spread fairly wide against informed traders and lean the quote up a little.

{"bid": 16.0, "ask": 21.5}

Fair value given public info is about **18.3**, so I'll quote bid 16.0 / ask 21.0, roughly centred there and nudged up slightly.

**Prior.** Die 1 averages 5.75 and die 2 averages 5, so the sum of the two hidden dice, T, averages 10.75. With die 3 revealed as 6, the prior fair value is 16.75.

**Updating on the trades.** I weighed all 24 combinations of die 1 and die 2 by how likely each makes the trades we saw. Each trade could come from an informed trader, with probability 0.2, or a noise trader, with probability 0.8.
- The buys at 19 and 20.5 favour high outcomes (T ≥ 14 and T ≥ 15). The noise-trader parts of these two likelihoods use public fair values I estimated, since the game's exact values aren't shown.
- The sell at 16 favours low outcomes (T ≤ 9), but less strongly.

The result is E[T] ≈ 12.3, so fair value ≈ 18.3.

**Quote.** The possible outcomes are lumpy and fairly spread out, so I keep the spread wide to limit losses to informed traders. Being short 1, I lean the quote slightly upward.

{"bid": 16.0, "ask": 21.0}

Dice 3 and 1 are revealed, so their total is 6 + 7 = 13, and the settlement is 13 plus die 2.

**Possible settlements.** Die 2 can be 1, 2, 3, 4, 8 or 12, each with probability 1/6. So the settlement is 14, 15, 16, 17, 21 or 25, with mean 18. Nobody has traded yet in stage 3, so the public fair value is 18.

**How the informed trader behaves.** It buys from me when the value is above my ask, which can only happen at 21 or 25. It sells to me when the value is below my bid, which can only happen at 14 to 17.

**Ask side.** Expected profit = 0.8·P(noise > a)·(a − 18) + 0.2·(1/6)·Σ(a − value) over the values above a.

| Ask | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 21 | about 0.65 |
| 22 | about 0.77 |
| 23 | about 0.83 |
| 23.5 | about 0.84 |
| 24 | about 0.84 |

The curve is flat between 23 and 24, so I pick 23.5.

**Bid side.** A bid at 14 or below never trades with the informed trader, because no value is below 14.

| Bid | Expected profit |
|---|---|
| 12 | about 0.87 |
| 13 | about 0.90 |
| 14 | about 0.87 |
| 14.5 | about 0.82 (now loses a little to the informed trader at value 14) |

The best bid is 13.

**Inventory.** My position is −2, which leaves room for two more sales before the ask is pulled, so the inventory limit doesn't constrain this quote.

{"bid": 13, "ask": 23.5}

Dice 3 and 1 are revealed (6 + 7 = 13), so settlement is 13 plus die 2. That gives possible values of 14, 15, 16, 17, 21 or 25.

**Updating on the trade history.** I weighted each die-2 value by how likely it made the trades and no-trades so far, given that 20% of counterparties are informed:
- The buys at 19, 20.5 and 21 favour the high values (8 and 12).
- The sale at 16 and some of the no-trade quotes pull back towards the low values.

The resulting probabilities are roughly:

| Settlement | 14 | 15 | 16 | 17 | 21 | 25 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 12% | 12% | 13.5% | 13.5% | 29.5% | 20% |

That puts expected die 2 near 6.1, so fair value is about 19.1.

**Choosing the quotes.** Wide quotes work best here because the possible values cluster at the extremes:
- **Ask:** an ask just below 25 is hit by informed traders only in the 25 case, and then loses less than 1 per unit. Noise traders still buy about 19–20% of the time, at a profit of about 5.5. The expected value of the ask side is about +0.87.
- **Bid:** a bid at 14 is never hit by an informed trader at a loss, since the lowest possible value is 14. Noise traders sell about 22% of the time, at a profit of about 5. The expected value of the bid side is about +0.9.
- **Position:** I am short 2, which leaves room on both sides within the ±4 limit.

{"bid": 14, "ask": 24.5}

Die 3 = 6 and die 1 = 7 are known, so the settlement is 13 + die 2. That gives six possible values, each equally likely before trading: 14, 15, 16, 17, 21 or 25. Die 2 averages 5, so the starting fair value is 18.

**Updating on stage 3 trading**
- **Quote 7 (13 / 23.5, no trade):** an informed trader would have bought if the value were 25. That outcome now gets weight 0.696 instead of 1 (0.8 × 0.573 = 0.458 versus 0.658 for the other values).
- **Quote 8 (sold at 14):** no informed trader values the contract below 14, so this sale must be noise. It tells us nothing about die 2.
- **Fair value:** about 17.6. I ignored the stage 1–2 trades; they point both ways and are hard to separate from die 1 and die 3.

**Choosing the ask**
Expected profit is noise profit minus informed loss:

| Ask | Noise profit | Informed loss | Net |
|---|---|---|---|
| 21 | 0.82 | 0.13 | 0.69 |
| 22 | 0.89 | 0.10 | 0.79 |
| 23 | 0.89 | 0.07 | 0.83 |
| 24 | 0.85 | 0.03 | 0.82 |

The best ask is about 23 to 24, so I quote 23.5.

**Choosing the bid**
At a bid of 14 or below, informed traders never sell. Among those bids, noise profit peaks around 13 (about 0.89). It is 0.84 at a bid of 14 and 0.89 at 12, so I bid 13.

This is the last quote, so my -1 position doesn't change the choice. Each side is set only on expected profit.

{"bid": 13, "ask": 23.5}
